Sūtapurāṇika
(‘narrator of पुराणस्, who was a सूत’)
------------------------------------------
See LOMAHARṢANA.

sūta
------------------------------------------
A सूत was one who was born to a क्षत्त्रिय ड़थेर् and a ब्राह्मण मोथेर्.
His occupation was to drive the chariot of the king, to cook for him, take care of his elephants and horses, and tender him suitable advice on kingly duties.
It was also his duty to serve the ब्राह्मणस्.
Another important function assigned to him was to maintain the vaṁśavṛkṣa (pedigrees) of kings.
He was also free to practise as a vaidya (doctor), after getting duly qualified.

Sutīkṣṇa
(‘one who was exceedingly sharp’)
------------------------------------------
Sutīkṣna was one of the many sages that राम met during his sojourn through the दण्डक forest. Though he had earned the passage to हेअवेन् and was invited by इन्द्र the ruler of हेअवेन्, he refused to go since he was eagerly waiting to meet राम and feel blessed.
He is said to have been a disciple of the great sage अगस्त्य and had saved the सोउल् of an evil person Durpaṇya by sprinkling the sacred water he had with him.

sūtaka
(‘[impurity] due to birth or death’)
------------------------------------------
See AŚAUCA.

Sūtasaṁhitā
(‘teaching of सूत’)
------------------------------------------
The Sūtasaṁhitā, though not very well-known, is an important religio-philosophical work. It is considered a part of the Skāndapurāṇa. However, the printed version of the purāṇa as available now, does not contain it.
It is divided into six sections containing a total of 109 adhyāyas (chapters) and 6044 ślokas (verses).
The following table gives an idea of the work:
Section Title Chapters Ślokas
1. Śivamāhātmyakhaṇḍa 13 721
2. Jñānayogakhaṇḍa 20 737
3. Muktikhaṇḍa 9 568
4. Yajñavaibhavakhaṇḍa 47 2502
5. Brahmagītā 12 1058
6. Sūtagītā 8 458

Total : 6 sections; 109 chapters; 6044 verses
Sometimes, the last two sections—the Brahmagītā and the Sūtagītā—are considered extensions of the Yajña-vaibhavakhaṇḍa itself.
Though the Sūtasaṁhitā is clearly devoted to the glorification of शिव and the शिव cult, other deities like विष्णु, ब्रह्मा and शक्ति (Divine मोथेर्) also get their honourable place. The basic spirit that all are manifestations of the same Supreme God is kept up.
A brief synopsis of the contents may now be presented here:
1. Śivamāhātmyakhaṇḍa
Description of the पुराणस्; performance of pāśupatavrata to please शिव; methods of worshipping शिव; need to get the grace of पराशक्ति (Pārvatī, the Divine मोथेर्); various spiritual paths leading to मुक्ति or लिबेरतिओन्, on time as also प्रलय (dissolution of the world); विष्णु saving भूदेवी (or the earth) in his इन्चर्नतिओन् as Varāha (Boar); details of च्रेअतिओन् by ब्रह्मा; manifestations of the four varṇas; on पिल्ग्रिमगे.
2. Jñānayogakhaṇḍa
Guruparamparā or the line of gurus through whom ज्ञानयोग was revealed; practice of the Aṣṭāṅga योग too needed; importance of the grace of शिव; details of the four āśramas viz., ब्रह्मचर्य, गार्हस्थ्य, वानप्रस्थ and सṁन्यास; prāyaścittas or expiations for sins, like कृच्छ्र and चान्द्रायण; on दान or giving gifts; various types of कर्म; narakas or hells; description of the various nāḍīs and चक्रस्; प्राणायाम; the eight steps of योग like यम and नियम; different kinds of āsanas like स्वस्तिक, गोमुख, पद्म and so on; varieties of ध्यान (meditation) and समाधि (superconscious experience).
3. Muktikhaṇḍa
Mukti or लिबेरतिओन् can be got only by transcending māyā, which again is possible only by the grace of ईश्वर or शिव; four kinds of मुक्ति (sālokya, सामीप्य, sārūpya and सायुज्य); the last is the best; remnants of prārabdha; जीवन्मुक्ति and videhamukti; कर्म as indirect and ज्ञान as direct means of लिबेरतिओन्; even the jñāni can perform कर्म without selfish motives; परमेश्वर alone can give मुक्ति or लिबेरतिओन्; description of शिव as दक्षिणामूर्ति; obstacles to लिबेरतिओन् like hatred of शिव, the presence of the six internal enemies (like lust and anger), cheating the गुरु and so on; service to the गुरु and a jñāni helps in attaining मुक्ति; description of शिव as नटराज.
4. Yajñavaibhavakhaṇḍa
Meaning of the वेदस्; how the persons in the four āśramas attain the higher worlds after death; शिव and the पञ्चाक्षरी (five-lettered) मन्त्र (namaśśivāya); nature of māyā; various paths of sādhana lead to the same goal ultimately; three types of कर्म (nitya, naimittika, kāmya); any कर्म done as worship of शिव leads to purity; how speech is produced in our body; on प्रणव or ओङ्कार; on the Gāyatrīmantra; description of the ajapāmantra (so’ham); six-lettered मन्त्र of शिव (oṁ namaś-śivāya); various kinds of meditation, seeing ब्रह्मन् in them; six प्रमाणस् or ways of knowledge; five forms of शिव, viz., सद्योजात, वामदेव, Tatpuruṣa, अघोर and ईशान; Umā (Pārvatī) is the giver of ब्रह्मविद्या; means of getting ज्ञान like prayer, mantrajapa, होम, service to the गुरु, worship of शिवलिङ्ग, self-control and so on; importance of वैराग्य (detachment, renunciation); superiority of the Śaivā-gamas; path of ज्ञान superior to all other paths; various modes of spiritual sādhanas created by शिव himself through their founders and prophets; how to get शिव’s grace; some stories to illustrate it; on the Śivaliṅgas and modes of worship of शिव; hymn to शिव containing all the letters of the alphabet; methods of wearing भस्म or holy ash; जप of शिव’s names destroys sins; places of पिल्ग्रिमगे; on the various karmas that lead to cittaśuddhi or purity of मिन्द्; evil effects of sins; advaita doctrine supported but other views also respected; prāyaścittas or expiations; on आत्मज्ञान; rules about purity of ड़ोओद्; prognostication regarding one’s death; diseases brought about by sins and how to overcome them.
5. Brahmagītā
Prayer of the gods to ब्रह्मा requesting him to teach them the true meaning of the वेदस्; his teaching begins; च्रेअतिओन् of the world by आत्मन् endowed with the special power māyā; all gods are different manifestations of परमेश्वर (Supreme God); need to perform karmas prescribed in the वेदस् and smṛtis; means of knowing; on the पञ्चकोशस् (five sheaths for the आत्मन्, the सोउल्); आनन्द or bliss is the true nature of ब्रह्मन्; essence of Kenopaniṣad explained; essence of the Chāndogyopaniṣad; meaning of tat-tvam-asi; daharākāśa or the small space in the region of the heart wherein आत्मन् is realised; parā (higher) and aparā (lower) विद्या (knowledge); meditation on the प्रणव or ओङ्कार; identity of the जीव (individual सोउल्) and परमात्मन् (the Supreme सोउल्); three states of चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स् (jāgrat etc.); all objects are dear because of the आत्मन् in them; all systems of philosophies reveal some aspect of the Truth; but Advaita is the highest; the varṇāśrama system and service to the गुरु help in spiritual evolution; upāsanā or meditation on Om; शिव is the highest गुरु.
6. Sūtagītā
Śaunaka and other sages approach the सूत to teach them spiritual wisdom; सूत meditates on his गुरु व्यास, who appears there, blesses him and permits him to transmit the same; the 36 principles of शैविस्म्; च्रेअतिओन् of the world by सदाशिव, the paratattva or the Highest Principle; difference between the jīvātman (individual सोउल्) and the परमात्मन् (God); other schools of philosophy; superiority of Advaita; more details about च्रेअतिओन्; nature of the आत्मन्; limitations of the jīvas; māyā and its three guṇas; ब्रह्मा, विष्णु and रुद्र are beyond māyā; in praise of the Atharvaveda as described in the Atharvaśikha Upaniṣad; about the abhimāni-देवतास् or deities presiding over various parts of the body; body being the means for attaining मोक्ष or लिबेरतिओन्, should be treated with respect and utilised properly; gradation of the paths described in the तन्त्रस्, smṛtis and the Śruti, the last being the best; all can get लिबेरतिओन् through the grace of God and by cultivating भक्ति (devotion) and श्रद्धा (faith) as per the directions given by the गुरु.

Sutala
------------------------------------------
The third of the nether worlds, सुतल has given shelter to बलि, the king of दानवस् (demons), after he was pushed down by Lord विष्णु in his इन्चर्नतिओन् as वामन. He spends most of his time in worshipping the Lord.
Lord विष्णु is guarding his palace, with the गदा (mace) in his hand.

Śutudrī
------------------------------------------
A river of the Vedic times, it has been mentioned twice in the Ṛgveda (3.33.1; 10.75.5). The word means ‘that which flows very fast’.
It is the easternmost river flowing in Punjab and has been identified with the modern Sutlej river.
During post-Vedic period the name got changed to Śatadrū.
According to the Mahābhārata this river was originally known as हैमवती. When the king कल्माषपाद, who had become a demon due to a curse, ate up all the sons of the sage वसिष्ठ, वसिष्ठ out of intense sorrow fell into this river to commit सुइचिदे. However, being afraid of killing such a great sage, the river broke into a hundred streams and carried him safely to the bank! Since then it came to be known as Śatadrū (vide Ādiparva 177).
See NADĪ also.
